Android

Add our repository in F-Droid, Droid-ify or Neo Store (Settings → Repositories → Add), or let Obtainium track the GitHub releases. Both update the app with every new stable release.

https://apps2samsung.com/fdroid/repo

Add to Obtainium

iPhone (beta)

Not on the App Store: install SideStore once, add our source under Sources, then install Apps2Samsung from it. A free Apple ID works. Allow Local Network access when iOS asks, or the app can't find your TV.

https://apps2samsung.com/sidestore/beta/apps.json

️ Desktop formats

Windows: .msi installer or a portable .zip. macOS: .dmg (Apple Silicon and Intel). Linux: .AppImage that runs anywhere without root, plus .deb, .rpm and a plain .tar.gz, in x64 and ARM64. Arch Linux: apps2samsung on the AUR, updated with every stable release. Command line: apps2samsung-cli for every platform, in the same releases.

The list above shows the newest stable release. The iPhone app and other beta builds ship first and carry the newest features; grab one from the releases page, or switch the in-app updater to the beta channel in Settings.

A little more on TV.

Your media server. Your PC games. Your favorite streams. Browse 110+ community apps, or install your own WGT or TPK package.

Community catalog

Jellyfin

The open-source media system, straight from jeppevinkel's Tizen builds (SmartHub, OSA, GrayFix, OblongIcon...), plus the AVPlay variants and a 10.8.z build for older sets. Tick Show all Jellyfin versions to choose from the newest five instead of just the latest.

Moonfin

A premium Jellyfin and Emby client built with the Enact framework for Samsung Smart TVs.

Litefin

Lightweight Jellyfin client for a premium feel even on legacy hardware.

Pelagica & Fladder

More Jellyfin clients: a modern web/TV client, and a Flutter-built native .tpk.

Moonlight

Low-latency game streaming (NVIDIA GameStream / Sunshine), including the no-gamemode and Tizen 5.5+ forks.

Chiaki

PlayStation Remote Play on the big screen, open source.

TizenTube

YouTube without ads, with SponsorBlock support.

TizenBrew

Modded websites and newer apps without fighting Tizen Studio.

RetroArch & Steam Link

Emulators on the TV, or stream your Steam library from your PC.

TVapp

IPTV player: configure your own m3u8 channels and their order before installing. The community fork fixes channel switching.

FCast, Beam-TV & RTSP viewer

Cast to the TV, play USB/DLNA media, or put your IP cameras on screen.

Custom WGT / TPK

Bring your own package, perfect for builds you maintain yourself. Native .tpk apps install too, not just web .wgt.

From here to your TV.

Get connected

Put your TV and computer or phone on the same network. Enable Developer Mode on the TV and enter your device's IP.

Find your TV

Open Apps2Samsung and scan your network. Choose your Samsung TV, projector, or smart monitor, or enter its IP manually.

Pick an app

Browse the catalog, choose a version, and fill in any settings it needs. Your Jellyfin server or IPTV channels can be ready at install.

Make it official

Sign in to Samsung to create the required signing certificate. Apps2Samsung installs the app and reuses that certificate next time.

Read the setup guide
Watch the Jellyfin installation walkthrough

Less setup.
More watching.

Discovery, signing, installation, and the useful things after. Open a feature to see what Apps2Samsung handles for you.

Automatic TV discovery

Scans your network and lists the Samsung TVs ready to receive an install, or type an IP manually. If a TV isn't ready, it tells you exactly why: Developer Mode off, wrong IP, reversed IP, or a TV that needs a power cycle.

Sign in to Samsung once

Generates the developer certificate for you and reuses it per TV. Pre-authorize extra TVs by DUID so one certificate covers them all, and switch between Public and Partner certificates when an app needs restricted privileges; it is turned on automatically when it's required.

A catalog you can browse

110+ apps in categories with search, a sheet per app with its description, versions or variants and source, and your favorites at the top. Adult apps stay hidden until you opt in, and apps that gain root on the TV are marked and ask before they install.

Asks what an app needs

An app that needs your own values, such as an API key, a server address or a port, gets a short form before it installs. Your answers are filled in again on the next update.

Manage what's installed

List the apps on a TV with their real icons and the catalog's newest version, update in one click, uninstall, launch or stop any of them, or force-remove a leftover package by id when an install went sideways.

Use it as a TV remote

D-pad, playback, volume, channel, power and typing straight from your phone or desktop, over Samsung's own remote channel, so it works on any TV on the network, Developer Mode or not.

Jellyfin, ready to watch

Bake in your server URL and auto-login, pick a JellyThemes community theme or your own CSS, set playback preferences, patch in supported server plugins and fix YouTube trailers (error 153), all at install time.

Your own IPTV channels

Add name + m3u8 stream pairs and their play order, validated and written into the TVapp package before it's installed.

Custom icons and titles

Give any app your own PNG launcher icon, a wide 16:9 tile for Tizen 5.5 sets, or a different name on the TV. Remembered per app and applied as it installs.

TV info and a real debug console

Read a TV's DUID, Tizen version, model and Developer Mode state, then launch any app in debug mode and watch it live, on the desktop and on the phone alike: the app's console, a packaged service's own log next to it, request timings that tell a slow download apart from slow decoding, and a query against an endpoint the app serves on the TV itself. Save or share the whole transcript.

Backup & restore

Export your settings and signing certificates to a single file and bring them to another PC, a Mac or your phone, with no second round of Samsung logins.

TV-Store (experimental)

Arm the TV-Store app from the TV toolbox once, and the TV browses and installs catalog apps by itself, with no PC or phone in the loop.

Command line

apps2samsung-cli runs the same scan, catalog, certificate and install steps from a terminal, a script or an AI agent, with JSON output on every command.

Resilient installs

Plain-language errors instead of Tizen codes: it spots active VPNs, subnet mismatches and certificates that aren't valid yet (with a countdown), and recovers from the common failures on its own.

Free & open source

MIT-licensed, no accounts, no telemetry. Built in the open on GitHub, with an in-app updater and an optional beta channel.

Before you start.

Samsung Tizen TVs, projectors, and smart monitors from roughly 2015 onward.

Need a hand? The wiki and Discord community can help.

Which TVs are supported?

Samsung Smart TVs, projectors and smart monitors running Tizen (roughly 2015 and newer). Older Orsay models are no longer supported; the unmaintained legacy Orsay installer remains available as-is.

Do I need a Samsung account?

Yes. Samsung's own developer flow requires signing in once so Apps2Samsung can create the signing certificate your TV needs. That certificate is then reused across installs, so you won't be asked again for the same TV. Installing to several TVs? Add their device IDs (DUIDs) in Settings and one certificate covers them all.

Do I need Developer Mode on the TV?

For installing, yes. Enable Developer Mode on your Samsung TV (Apps → type 12345 → toggle on, set your computer/phone's IP), then scan for it in Apps2Samsung. This is the standard Tizen side-loading requirement, and if something is off, the app tells you which part. The remote does not need Developer Mode.

Does the remote need Developer Mode too?

No. The remote rides Samsung's own remote-control channel, so it works on any TV that's awake on the same network, including sets you can't install to. The first connection asks you to accept a prompt on the TV; after that it's silent, and the app can even wake a sleeping TV over the network.

Is this safe? Is it official?

Apps2Samsung uses Samsung's own developer/side-load mechanism, the same one Tizen Studio uses, so it doesn't jailbreak or modify your TV's firmware. It's fully open source, so you can read exactly what it does. It isn't affiliated with Samsung or Jellyfin.

Is there an iPhone app?

Yes, as a beta. It has the same screens as the Android app and installs through SideStore with your own Apple ID; a free one works, and SideStore refreshes it every 7 days. Add https://apps2samsung.com/sidestore/beta/apps.json as a source in SideStore. Please report what you find in #753.

Which Linux package should I take?

The AppImage if you're not sure: it runs on any distro without root. Otherwise the .deb (Debian/Ubuntu), the .rpm (Fedora/openSUSE) or the .tar.gz. All four come in x64 and ARM64. On Arch Linux, install apps2samsung from the AUR (yay -S apps2samsung), published by our release workflow. On NixOS, clone the repo and run nix-shell.

Can I move my setup to another device?

Yes. Backup & restore exports your settings and signing certificates to one file that you can import on another PC, a Mac or your phone, so you don't have to sign in to Samsung again.

What languages does it speak?

30, all fully translated: from Dutch, German and French to Japanese, Arabic, Ukrainian and both Chinese scripts. It follows your system language and can be switched at any time in Settings. Help out on Crowdin.

What does it cost?

Nothing. It's free and MIT-licensed, with no accounts or telemetry. If it saved you time, a coffee is always appreciated.

Can I add my own app?

Absolutely: use the Custom WGT/TPK option to install a local package, web or native. Community apps live in the open tizen-community-packages repo, and contributions are welcome.

Something went wrong. Where do I get help?

The app can export a debug log (Settings → Backup and diagnostics) to attach to a report. Then open an issue, check the wiki FAQ, or come and ask on Discord.

A community project. Open to everyone.
